subproblems.title: Support lemma (Simon 6.2.11): a current vanishes on test forms supported away from its support (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be a current in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n: a sequentially continuous linear functional on the space 𝒟ⁿ(U) of smooth n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). The support of S is spt S = U ∖ Z_S, where Z_S is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11, as formalized by GeometricCurrentOn.support). If tsupport ω ∩ spt S = ∅, then S(ω) = 0. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_vanish_off_support (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.vanish_off_support-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 2.11 (chapter-06.txt lines 296–301) and the standard partition-of-unity argument; Simon uses this property tacitly (e.g. in 2.12). Write 𝒲 for the family of open sets W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and S vanishing on W (S(η) = 0 whenever η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport η ⊆ W); thus Z_S = ⋃𝒲 and spt S = U ∖ Z_S.
1. Since ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ω is smooth with compact support, so C := tsupport ω is compact, and C ⊆ U. If C = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume C ≠ ∅.
2. From C ⊆ U and C ∩ (U ∖ Z_S) = ∅ we get C ⊆ Z_S = ⋃𝒲. The members of 𝒲 are open and C is compact, so there are W_1, …, W_N ∈ 𝒲 with C ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_N.
3. Choose a smooth partition of unity on the compact (hence closed) set C subordinate to the open cover (W_i)_{i≤N}: C^∞ functions χ_1, …, χ_N : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport χ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_{i=1}^N χ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ C. (Such partitions exist on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P, e.g. Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate with the model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), or directly from smooth bump functions, Mathlib exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset.)
4. For each i put ω_i := χ_i ω, i.e. ω_i(x) = χ_i(x)·ω(x). Then ω_i is smooth and tsupport ω_i ⊆ tsupport χ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ C. Hence tsupport ω_i is compact and contained in U, so ω_i ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); and tsupport ω_i ⊆ W_i with W_i ∈ 𝒲, so S(ω_i) = 0.
5. Σ_{i=1}^N ω_i = ω pointwise: for x ∈ C, Σ_i χ_i(x)ω(x) = ω(x); for x ∉ C, ω(x) = 0 and hence ω_i(x) = 0 for all i. By linearity of S on 𝒟ⁿ(U), S(ω) = Σ_{i=1}^N S(ω_i) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U missing spt S = U ∖ Z_S, so finitely many open W_i (closure compact in U) on which S vanishes cover it.
A smooth partition of unity χ_i on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i splits ω = Σ χ_i ω, each χ_i ω a test form in U supported in W_i.
S(χ_i ω) = 0 for each i, hence S(ω) = 0 by linearity.

subproblems.title: Mass formula and support of an integer multiplicity current (Simon 6.3.2(3), 6.2.12) — reused accepted declaration
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, equal to ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Let μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3), 2.11–2.12. Notation: μ := μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (covectorEuclideanNorm; I strictly increasing multi-indices), dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}, ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ := ξ(x)(α).
1. Where R.orients holds at x ∈ M (Hⁿ-a.e. on M, so μ-a.e.), ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = s·Σ_I α(e_I)det(τ^I) with τ orthonormal, s = ±1 (multilinearity, alternation; τ^I = rows I of the matrix of τ), and Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1 (Cauchy–Binet). So |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Schwarz), and ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), so |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ (n = 0: I = ∅, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1). ξ^♭ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (continuous linear in ξ; R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: a.e. strongly measurable, zero off the compact spt ω ⊆ U, a.e. bounded by θ·sup|ω| (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). So T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩dμ.
3. For open W and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), ⟨ω, ξ⟩ ≤ 1 μ-a.e. (step 1) and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ(W) (step 2). So M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
4. For real t < μ(W) (μ(W) = ∞ allowed) we find admissible ω with T(ω) > t. G := W ∩ U is open and σ-compact, μ(G) = μ(W) (M ⊆ U), and μ, finite on compacts of U, is Radon on G (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15): inner regular by compacts, outer regular on finite-measure sets. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon 1.17): a compact K' ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ K') < η, ξ^♭|K' continuous, |ξ^♭| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ μ-a.e. on K'. (b) An open V ⊇ K' with V̄ ⊆ G compact, μ(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend ξ^♭|K' coefficientwise continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), retract radially onto the closed |·|-unit ball of Λⁿ(ℝ^P), multiply by a continuous χ: ℝ^P → [0, 1], χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V: g is continuous, spt g ⊆ V compact, |g| ≤ 1, g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise, standard mollifier): for 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V) it is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)|dy ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm), and g_ε → g uniformly; so g_ε is admissible. (e) With δ_ε := sup|g_ε − g|·μ(V̄) → 0 (μ(V̄) < ∞), steps 2, 1 give T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩dμ ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩dμ − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩|dμ − δ_ε ≥ μ(K') − η − δ_ε ≥ μ(K) − 2η − δ_ε > t + 2η − δ_ε > t for small ε. With step 3 this is (i).
5. spt T = U ∖ Z (GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11), Z the union of the open W with W̄ ⊆ U compact and T(ω) = 0 whenever spt ω ⊆ W; x ∈ spt μ iff μ(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ lay in such a W, then M_W(T) = 0, so μ(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ; so U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ, take r > 0 with μ(B_r(x)) = 0, B̄_r(x) ⊆ U; by step 2 T(ω) = 0 whenever spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), so x ∈ Z, x ∉ spt T. Hence (ii).
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet: |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., and ξ^♭ satisfies |ξ^♭| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩.
Integral formula T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
Upper bound: admissible ω give T(ω) ≤ μ(W), so M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
Lower bound: Lusin, Tietze, radial retraction, cutoff and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) > t for each real t < μ(W).
Support: by (i) and the integral formula, the zero region Z of T is U ∖ spt μ, so spt T = U ∩ spt μ.

subproblems.title: Calculus of integer multiplicity representations: locality of approximate tangent spaces, restriction, differences, orientation bound (reused accepted declaration; the parent's (IMC))
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm). This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.im_calculus-a1), which is reused; its type is also byte-identical to the second conjunct of the parent's sibling foundations, cited in the parent proof as (IMC).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: comparator-accepted declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub; parts (b)–(d) are the parent proof's (IMC)(b)–(d). Its audited proof follows.
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
Hence for every f the two families of integrals have the same limit as r → 0⁺ or both have none; the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for every x ∈ M ∖ Z' and every Q; the exceptional set M ∩ Z' is null for Hⁿ⌞M. ∎

(b) Restriction. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in the open set U and E a Borel set. Define R' with carrier M ∩ E and the same mult θ and orient ξ.
1. Structure fields: M ∩ E is Borel and contained in U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation: by (P6) and (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E and all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. With the orientation field of R (Hⁿ-a.e. on M) this gives the orientation field of R'.
3. The current: A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and uniform convergence of all derivatives, in particular |ω_j|_∞ → 0 since all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent), then |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n and R' represents A (IMRep.Represents, IMRep.action). ∎

(c) Differences. Let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, be represented by R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A) and R_B = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B).
1. (Borel versions and good points.) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability; set them 0 off the carriers). Let G be the set of x ∈ M_A ∪ M_B such that: if x ∈ M_A, then ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x) and there is Q_A(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_A x Q_A(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_A x) Q_A(x); the analogous condition for B if x ∈ M_B; and, for each pair (N, N') among (M_A ∩ M_B, M_A), (M_A ∩ M_B, M_B) with x ∈ N, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q for every Q. By the orientation fields of R_A, R_B, by (P6) and by (a), (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ ⊇ (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0).
2. (Overlap.) Let x ∈ (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀. The approximate tangent space of M_A ∩ M_B at x exists and equals Q_A(x) and also Q_B(x) (the equivalences defining G and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique); so Q_A(x) = Q_B(x) and by (P5) ξ̃_B(x) = ε(x)ξ̃_A(x) with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. Put ε(x) := 1 if ξ̃_B(x) = ξ̃_A(x) and ε(x) := −1 otherwise (a Borel function).
3. (Data.) Put O := (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀, k := θ_A − εθ_B ∈ ℤ on O, and
 M := ((M_A ∖ M_B) ∪ (M_B ∖ M_A) ∪ {x ∈ O : k(x) ≠ 0}) ∖ N₀,
 θ := θ_A on M_A ∖ M_B, θ_B on M_B ∖ M_A, |k| on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued),
 ζ := ξ̃_A on M_A ∖ M_B, −ξ̃_B on M_B ∖ M_A, sign(k)ξ̃_A on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel).
For every x ∉ N₀: θ(x)1_M(x)ζ(x) = θ_A(x)1_{M_A}(x)ξ̃_A(x) − θ_B(x)1_{M_B}(x)ξ̃_B(x) (on O with k = 0 both sides vanish; on O with k ≠ 0, θ_Aξ̃_A − θ_Bεξ̃_A = kξ̃_A = |k| sign(k)ξ̃_A; the other cases are immediate).
4. (Representation.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), integrating ⟨ω, ·⟩ against both sides of step 3 (N₀ is null; all integrands are integrable by (d), since θ1_M ≤ θ_A1_{M_A} + θ_B1_{M_B}):
 ∫_M θ⟨ω, ζ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M_A} θ_A⟨ω, ξ_A⟩ dHⁿ − ∫_{M_B} θ_B⟨ω, ξ_B⟩ dHⁿ = A(ω) − B(ω) = (A − B)(ω).
5. (Structure fields.) M is Borel, M ⊆ M_A ∪ M_B ⊆ U, and M is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_iUnion, CountablyRectifiable.mono). θ is Borel and ℕ-valued with θ ≥ 1 on M (|k| ≥ 1 where k ≠ 0), and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M_A∩K} θ_A dHⁿ + ∫_{M_B∩K} θ_B dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
6. (Orientation.) For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M_A ∩ K) + Hⁿ(M_B ∩ K) < ∞ by (P6) applied to R_A, R_B. Apply (a) to the pairs (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M_A), (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M_B), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M) (all Borel, contained in U, with locally finite Hⁿ-measure): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ M_A the approximate tangent spaces of M and of M_A at x coincide (both equal that of M ∩ M_A), and similarly for M_B. Let x be such a point, x ∉ N₀. If x ∈ M_A, then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_A(x) and ζ(x) = ±ξ_A(x) (cases M_A ∖ M_B and O, using ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x)), a unit orientation of Q_A(x) by (P5). If x ∈ M_B ∖ M_A, ζ(x) = −ξ_B(x) is a unit orientation of Q_B(x), the approximate tangent space of M at x. Hence the orientation field holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M.
So (M, θ, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing A − B, and A − B is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: (d): Cauchy–Binet gives Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = 1 for orthonormal τ, so |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
(a): the density of Hⁿ⌞(M′∖M) vanishes at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6 on an exhaustion of U), so the blow-up integrals of M and M′ have the same limits.
(b): all IMRep fields restrict; the orientation field transfers by (a); continuity of the restricted current from local integrability and (d).
(c): on the overlap the approximate tangent spaces agree a.e., so the orientations differ by a sign; combine multiplicities θ_A ∓ θ_B, drop cancellation points, and verify the IMRep fields with (a).

subproblems.title: Restriction of an integer multiplicity current to an open subdomain is integer multiplicity (reused accepted declaration; the parent's (F5))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and V ⊆ U ⊆ ℝ^P with V open. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity, i.e. T = τ(M, θ, ξ) for some IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) of U (Simon 6.3.1). Then the restriction T⌞V ∈ 𝒟_n(V) is integer multiplicity in V. Here T⌞V = T.restrictDomain, T⌞V(ω) = T(ιω) with ι = testFormOnInclusion. Explicitly, T⌞V is represented by (M ∩ V, θ, ξ). This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.restrict_im-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V : Set (Euclid P)) (hVU : V ⊆ U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen V → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsIntegerMultiplicity (T.restrictDomain hVU)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (F5) of the parent proof (the domain restriction X|_V of an integer multiplicity current is integer multiplicity, represented by the restricted triple), Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753) and Ch. 3, 1.4. Reused accepted declaration dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity; the proof below is its audited proof, except that the citation of a lemma of its original branch in step 7 is replaced by the elementary locality of approximate tangent spaces at points of the open set V.
Let R = (M, θ, ξ) = (R.carrier, R.mult, R.orient) be an IMRep of U with R.Represents T. Define R′ with carrier M ∩ V, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. We check the fields of IMRep V n, then the representation.
1. Measurability: M is Borel and V is open, so M ∩ V is Borel.
2. M ∩ V ⊆ V.
3. Rectifiability: M ∩ V ⊆ M, and M is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
4. θ is measurable, and θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M ∩ V ⊆ M.
5. Local integrability in V. Let K be compact with K ⊆ V. Then (M ∩ V) ∩ K = M ∩ K because K ⊆ V. Also K ⊆ V ⊆ U, so ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the local integrability of R in U.
6. ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V), because Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono; AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure).
7. Orientation. By the field orients of R, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. A property holding Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. also holds Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset), and Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ V (ae_restrict_mem). Fix such an x ∈ M ∩ V and its Q; we show HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ V) x Q. The condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P); choose ρ > 0 with f = 0 outside B_ρ(0) and δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ V (V is open). For r > 0 let η_r(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r), a homeomorphism of ℝ^P, so that η_r(M) and η_r(M ∩ V) are Borel and η_r(M ∩ V) ⊆ η_r(M). For 0 < r < δ/ρ: if y ∈ M and η_r(y) ∈ B_ρ(0), then |y − x| < rρ < δ, so y ∈ V; hence η_r(M) ∖ η_r(M ∩ V) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ B_ρ(0), where f = 0, and therefore ∫_{η_r(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} f dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero). The two functions of r agree on (0, δ/ρ), a set belonging to the filter 𝓝[>] 0, so they have the same limit ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺. As f was arbitrary, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ V) x Q holds, and the same Q still satisfies IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Hence R′ is an IMRep of V.
8. Representation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V). The form ιω (testFormOnInclusion) has the same underlying form, so (T⌞V)(ω) = T(ιω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x). For x ∈ M ∖ (M ∩ V) we have x ∉ V ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and the integrand θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) vanishes (ξ(x) is linear). M is measurable and M ∩ V ⊆ M, so ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩V} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero), and the right side is R′.action ω. Thus R′ represents T⌞V, and T⌞V is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict a representation (M, θ, ξ) of T to (M ∩ V, θ, ξ): measurability, rectifiability, positivity and local integrability on compact subsets of V ⊆ U are inherited.
At x ∈ V, for r < δ/ρ the blow-ups η_r(M) and η_r(M ∩ V) coincide on B_ρ(0) ⊇ spt f, so M and M ∩ V have the same approximate tangent space at x; the orientation field transfers.
Forms supported in V vanish on M ∖ V, so the integral over M equals the integral over M ∩ V.

subproblems.title: Measure calculus of an integer multiplicity representation and of its restrictions to Borel sets (reused accepted declaration; the parent's (F4))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (contract IMRep U n) with weight μ_R := θ Hⁿ⌞M (contract R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then (a) μ_R is absolutely continuous with respect to Hⁿ⌞M; (b) ξ is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable; (c) for every Borel set E and every IMRep R′ in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ: μ_{R′} = μ_R⌞E, and for every n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ (no regularity assumed) the action R′(ω) = ∫_{M∩E} θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (contract IMRep.action) equals ∫_E ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dμ_R(x) (Bochner integrals). This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration lcmp_imRep_measure_restrict (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.imrep_restriction-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), R.measure ≪ μHE[n].restrict R.carrier ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable R.orient R.measure ∧ ∀ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (R' : IMRep U n), MeasurableSet E → R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E → R'.mult = R.mult → R'.orient = R.orient → R'.measure = R.measure.restrict E ∧ ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, R'.action ω = ∫ x in E, R.orient x (ω x) ∂R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (F4) of the parent proof (“μ_{A⌞E} = μ_A⌞E”; “(R.measure, R.orient) is a representation as in (SL) … the currents ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ of (SL) are exactly the A⌞E”). This child isolates the measure-theoretic identities behind these sentences; they hold for every IMRep (openness of U is not needed). Reused accepted declaration lcmp_imRep_measure_restrict; its audited proof follows.

Notation: ν := Hⁿ⌞M, so μ_R = ν.withDensity θ, where θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is Borel (IMRep field measurable_mult) and is used as a density through the cast ℕ → [0, ∞).

1. (a) A measure with a density with respect to ν is absolutely continuous with respect to ν (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous): if ν(N) = 0 then μ_R(N) = ∫_N θ dν = 0.
2. (b) The IMRep field aestronglyMeasurable_orient says that ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν. By (a), every ν-null set is μ_R-null, so ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ_R (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac).
3. (c), weights. Let E be Borel and R′ as in the statement. Restriction to a measurable set commutes with taking a density, and restrictions compose: (ν.withDensity θ)⌞E = (ν⌞E).withDensity θ (restrict_withDensity) and ν⌞E = (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞E = Hⁿ⌞(E ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence μ_R⌞E = (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)).withDensity θ = μ_{R′}, because R′ has carrier M ∩ E and multiplicity θ.
4. (c), actions. The map x ↦ θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞) is Borel (a Borel map into ℕ followed by a map out of the discrete space ℕ). For any measure λ, any Borel density g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞) and any function h : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ h d(λ.withDensity g) = ∫ g·h dλ as Bochner integrals, without any integrability assumption (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul; if one side is not integrable, neither is the other and both integrals are 0). Apply this with λ = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E), g = θ and h(x) = ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩: by step 3, ∫_E ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_{R′} = ∫_{M∩E} θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ, and the last integral is R′(ω) by the definition of IMRep.action for R′ (carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ, orientation ξ). ∎
proof_key_steps: μ_R = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, hence ξ is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable.
(ν.withDensity θ)⌞E = (ν⌞E).withDensity θ and (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞E = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E), so μ_R⌞E = μ_{R′}.
∫ h d(λ.withDensity θ) = ∫ θ h dλ (no integrability needed) turns ∫_E ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R into ∫_{M∩E} θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = R′(ω).

subproblems.title: Triangle inequality for local mass (reused accepted declaration; the parent's (F3) for open sets)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U, G ⊆ ℝ^P, X, Y, Z ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (contract GeometricCurrentOn U k) and c ∈ ℝ with |c| ≤ 1, and suppose Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G. Then M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y), where M_G is the SimonGMT local mass massOn (supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.mass_triangle-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U G : Set (Euclid P)) (X Y Z : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (c : ℝ), |c| ≤ 1 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ⊆ G → Z ω = X ω + c * Y ω) → Z.massOn G ≤ X.massOn G + Y.massOn G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (F3) of the parent proof (“ofReal((A±B)(ω)) ≤ ofReal(A(ω)) + ofReal(±B(ω)) for admissible ω; −ω is admissible”), with the identity required only for forms supported in G, as in step 8(d) of the parent (there the identity holds only for tsupport ω ⊆ W). Reused accepted declaration lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq; its audited proof follows.

1. Let ω be admissible for M_G: ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Then −ω is admissible as well: tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω, and |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| because the Euclidean coefficient norm is invariant under α ↦ −α (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. By the definition of M_G as a supremum, ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ M_G(X), ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ M_G(Y) and ofReal(Y(−ω)) ≤ M_G(Y); by linearity Y(−ω) = −Y(ω). Hence ofReal(|Y(ω)|) ≤ M_G(Y) (|Y(ω)| is Y(ω) or −Y(ω)).
3. c·Y(ω) ≤ |c·Y(ω)| = |c|·|Y(ω)| ≤ |Y(ω)|, so by hypothesis Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) ≤ X(ω) + |Y(ω)|. Since ofReal is monotone and ofReal(p + q) ≤ ofReal(p) + ofReal(q) for all real p, q (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le): ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ ofReal(X(ω)) + ofReal(|Y(ω)|) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y).
4. Taking the supremum over all admissible ω gives M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y). ∎
proof_key_steps: For ω admissible in G, −ω is admissible too, so ofReal(|Y(ω)|) ≤ M_G(Y).
c·Y(ω) ≤ |Y(ω)| since |c| ≤ 1, so ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ ofReal(X(ω)) + ofReal(|Y(ω)|) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y).
Take the supremum over admissible ω.

subproblems.title: Passing a measure inequality from compactly contained open neighbourhoods to a compact set (reused accepted declaration; the parent's (F3) beyond open sets)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, E ⊆ U compact, μ and ν measures on ℝ^P with ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and c ∈ [0, ∞]. Suppose μ(G) ≤ ν(G) + c for every open G ⊇ E such that closure(G) is compact and contained in U. Then μ(E) ≤ ν(E) + c. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration lcmp_measure_le_add_of_open_nhds (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.compact_outer_bound-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U E : Set (Euclid P)) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (c : ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen U → IsCompact E → E ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ν K < ∞) → (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → E ⊆ G → CompactlyContained G U → μ G ≤ ν G + c) → μ E ≤ ν E + c
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (F3) of the parent proof (from open sets to other Borel sets by outer regularity of the finite restricted measures), needed for the compact sets Σ_α = {ψ_c = α} (step 8(c)) and the sphere ∂B_G (step 7(e)). It passes an inequality between measures from open neighbourhoods of a compact set to the set itself by continuity from above. Reused accepted declaration lcmp_measure_le_add_of_open_nhds; its audited proof follows.

1. If E = ∅ then μ(E) = 0 and there is nothing to prove; the argument below also covers this case. Choose δ > 0 with C_δ := {x : dist(x, E) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). For k ∈ ℕ put r_k := δ/(k + 2) ∈ (0, δ) and G_k := {x : dist(x, E) < r_k} (open thickening).
2. Each G_k is open and contains E (r_k > 0). closure(G_k) ⊆ {dist(·, E) ≤ r_k} ⊆ C_δ ⊆ U, and C_δ is compact (closed thickening of a compact set in the proper space ℝ^P), so closure(G_k) is compact and contained in U. By hypothesis and monotonicity, μ(E) ≤ μ(G_k) ≤ ν(G_k) + c for every k.
3. Since r_k decreases, (G_k) is decreasing. ⋂_k G_k = E: E ⊆ G_k for all k; conversely, if dist(x, E) < r_k for all k, then for every ε > 0 some r_k < ε gives x ∈ {dist(·, E) < ε}, so x ∈ ⋂_{ε>0} {dist(·, E) < ε} = closure(E) (Metric.closure_eq_iInter_thickening) = E, E being compact and hence closed. The G_k are open, hence measurable, and ν(G_0) ≤ ν(C_δ) < ∞.
4. By continuity from above (Mathlib tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop), ν(G_k) → ν(E). Addition of the constant c is continuous on [0, ∞], so ν(G_k) + c → ν(E) + c, and letting k → ∞ in μ(E) ≤ ν(G_k) + c gives μ(E) ≤ ν(E) + c. ∎
proof_key_steps: δ > 0 with closed δ-thickening of E inside U; G_k := open δ/(k + 2)-thickening of E.
Each G_k is open, contains E and has compact closure in U, so μ(E) ≤ μ(G_k) ≤ ν(G_k) + c.

subproblems.title: Mass localization for a current vanishing away from a compact set (reused accepted declaration; step 5(a) of the parent)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U, V, C ⊆ ℝ^P with C compact, V open and C ⊆ V, and let X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) satisfy X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) whose topological support is disjoint from C. Then M_G(X) ≤ M_V(X) for every set G ⊆ ℝ^P (M_G = SimonGMT massOn with the Euclidean coefficient norm). This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration lcmp_massOn_le_of_vanish_off_compact (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.mass_localization-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U V C : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k), IsCompact C → IsOpen V → C ⊆ V → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) C → X ω = 0) → ∀ G : Set (Euclid P), X.massOn G ≤ X.massOn V
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5(a) of the parent proof (“let χ ∈ C_c^∞(W₀; [0, 1]), χ = 1 near the compact Σ_s ⊆ W₀. For open G and ω admissible for M_G, (1 − χ)ω vanishes near Σ_s, so P_{j,s}(ω) = P_{j,s}(χω) with χω admissible for M_{W₀}: M_G(P_{j,s}) ≤ M_{W₀}(P_{j,s})”), stated for an arbitrary current X, compact set C (= Σ_s) and open set V (= W₀); the argument works for every set G. Reused accepted declaration lcmp_massOn_le_of_vanish_off_compact; its audited proof follows.

Notation: |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a k-covector (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm); ω is admissible for M_G if ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; M_G(X) is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over admissible ω.

1. Case C = ∅. Every test form has support disjoint from ∅, so X(ω) = 0 for all ω; every term of the supremum defining M_G(X) is ofReal(0) = 0, so M_G(X) = 0 ≤ M_V(X).
2. Assume C ≠ ∅. Choose δ > 0 with {x : dist(x, C) ≤ δ} ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open) and let V′ := {x : dist(x, C) < δ/2}. V′ is open, C ⊆ V′, and closure(V′) ⊆ {x : dist(x, C) ≤ δ/2}, a compact set (closed thickening of a compact set) contained in V.
3. A smooth cut-off. Take g ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P) with values in [0, 1] and {g ≠ 0} = V′ (Mathlib IsOpen.exists_contDiff_support_eq). g is continuous and positive on the nonempty compact set C ⊆ V′, so a := min_C g > 0 (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). Let τ := Real.smoothTransition (smooth, 0 ≤ τ ≤ 1, τ = 0 on (−∞, 0], τ = 1 on [1, ∞)) and χ(x) := τ(2g(x)/a). Then χ is smooth and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1. On the open set N := {g > a/2} ⊇ C we have 2g/a > 1, so χ = 1 on N. Where g = 0 we have χ = τ(0) = 0, so {χ ≠ 0} ⊆ V′; hence tsupport χ ⊆ closure(V′) ⊆ V and χ has compact support.
4. Scaling of the norm. For c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector α, |cα| = |c|·|α|: the coefficients of cα on the increasing coordinate tuples are c times those of α, so the sum of their squares is c² times that of α, and √(c²s) = |c|√s.
5. Let ω be admissible for M_G and put ω₁ := χω, ω₂ := ω − ω₁ = (1 − χ)ω. ω₁ is smooth (product of smooth maps) and tsupport ω₁ ⊆ tsupport ω ∩ tsupport χ; hence ω₁ has compact support contained in U, i.e. ω₁ ∈ 𝒟^k(U), and tsupport ω₁ ⊆ V. By step 4, |ω₁(x)| = χ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ 1. So ω₁ is admissible for M_V and ofReal(X(ω₁)) ≤ M_V(X).
6. ω₂ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) vanishes on the open set N, because χ = 1 there. Every point of C has the neighbourhood N on which ω₂ ≡ 0, so no point of C lies in tsupport ω₂ = closure{ω₂ ≠ 0}; i.e. tsupport ω₂ is disjoint from C, and the hypothesis gives X(ω₂) = 0. By linearity X(ω) = X(ω₁) + X(ω₂) = X(ω₁), hence ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ M_V(X).
7. Taking the supremum over all admissible ω gives M_G(X) ≤ M_V(X). ∎
proof_key_steps: C = ∅: X vanishes identically, so M_G(X) = 0.
Smooth χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on an open N ⊇ C and compact tsupport χ ⊆ V: χ = τ(2g/a) with {g ≠ 0} = V′ ⋐ V and a = min_C g > 0.
For ω admissible in G: (1 − χ)ω vanishes on N, so X(ω) = X(χω); χω is admissible in V since |χω| = χ|ω| ≤ 1.
Hence ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ M_V(X); take the supremum.

subproblems.title: Choice of a good slicing level and of a subsequence (reused accepted declaration; step 5(c) of the parent)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let (ν_j)_{j∈ℕ} and (κ_j)_{j∈ℕ} be measures on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel measurable, a < b real and A := {x : a < f(x) < b}. Assume ν_j(A) < ∞ for every j, ν_j(A) → 0 as j → ∞, and κ_j(A) < ∞ for every j. Then there are t ∈ (a, b) and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that (i) κ_j({f = t}) = 0 for every j; (ii) D_j(t) < ∞ for every j; (iii) D_{φ(j)}(t) → 0 as j → ∞; where D_j(t) := liminf_{h → 0, h > 0} ofReal(h⁻¹)·ν_j({x : t − h < f(x) < t}) ∈ [0, ∞] (liminf along the filter 𝓝[>] 0). This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration lcmp_exists_good_slice_level (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.good_slice_level-a1), which is reused.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5(c) of the parent proof (Simon 7.2.4 (3)–(5), chapter-07.txt lines 192–205: “By the slicing theory (and in particular by 4.5 of Ch. 6) we can choose 0 < α < 1 and a subsequence … We can also of course choose α to be such that (5) …”). The sibling slice_decomposition applies this lemma with ν_j := μ_{R_j}⌞W₀, κ_j := κ_{j+j₁}, f := −ψ and (a, b) := (−1, 0), so that A = {0 < ψ < 1}, {t − h < f < t} = {α < ψ < α + h} and {f = t} = {ψ = α} for α := −t ∈ (0, 1); the slicing hypothesis bounds M_{W₀}(P_{j,α}) by L·D_j(t). Reused accepted declaration lcmp_exists_good_slice_level; its audited proof follows.
Detail (departure in the choice of the majorant). The parent majorizes the difference quotients by −L H_j′ with H_j(s) = μ_{R_j}(W₀ ∩ {s < ψ < 1}) and bounds ∫ −H_j′ by Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc; that lemma is not in the import closure of the frozen contract. We use instead the sequential lower difference quotient G_j below, whose integral bound follows from Tonelli's theorem; the remainder of the argument (Fatou's lemma, countably many atoms, choice of the level and of the subsequence) is the parent's.

All quantities lie in [0, ∞] (0·∞ = 0); λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and “a.e.” refers to λ.

1. Measurability. Since f is Borel, A, the level sets {f = s} and the sets {t − h < f < t} are Borel.
2. Pushforward. Let ρ_j be the image of ν_j⌞A under f: ρ_j(B) = ν_j(f⁻¹(B) ∩ A) for Borel B ⊆ ℝ. Then ρ_j(ℝ) = ν_j(A) < ∞, so ρ_j is a finite Borel measure on ℝ.
3. Tonelli. For c ∈ ℝ let S_c := {(s, y) ∈ ℝ² : s − c < y < s}, a Borel set. Its sections are {y : (s, y) ∈ S_c} = (s − c, s) and {s : (s, y) ∈ S_c} = (y, y + c). Hence s ↦ ρ_j((s − c, s)) is Borel (measurability of sections of a product set, Mathlib measurable_measure_prodMk_left), and computing (λ × ρ_j)(S_c) in both orders (Measure.prod_apply, Measure.prod_apply_symm) gives ∫ ρ_j((s − c, s)) dλ(s) = ∫ λ((y, y + c)) dρ_j(y) = ofReal(c)·ρ_j(ℝ) = ofReal(c)·ν_j(A).
4. Majorants. For k ∈ ℕ let h_k := 1/(k + 1) and F_{j,k}(s) := (k + 1)·ρ_j((s − h_k, s)). By step 3, F_{j,k} is Borel and ∫ F_{j,k} dλ = (k + 1)·ofReal(h_k)·ν_j(A) = ν_j(A). Let G_j(s) := liminf_{k→∞} F_{j,k}(s), a Borel function. Fatou's lemma gives ∫ G_j dλ ≤ liminf_k ∫ F_{j,k} dλ = ν_j(A) < ∞; hence G_j < ∞ a.e., and, intersecting countably many full-measure sets, a.e. s satisfies G_j(s) < ∞ for every j.
5. Fatou in j. H(s) := liminf_{j→∞} G_j(s) is Borel and ∫ H dλ ≤ liminf_j ∫ G_j dλ ≤ liminf_j ν_j(A) = 0, because ν_j(A) → 0. Hence H = 0 a.e.
6. Atoms. For each j the measure κ_j⌞A is finite. The level sets {f = s}, s ∈ ℝ, are pairwise disjoint, so (κ_j⌞A)({f = s}) > 0 for at most countably many s (Mathlib Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos). Countable sets are λ-null, so for a.e. s: (κ_j⌞A)({f = s}) = 0 for every j.
7. The level. λ((a, b)) = b − a > 0. By steps 4–6, a.e. s ∈ (a, b) satisfies H(s) = 0, G_j(s) < ∞ for every j, and (κ_j⌞A)({f = s}) = 0 for every j. A full-measure subset of a set of positive measure is nonempty, so there is t ∈ (a, b) with these three properties.
8. (i). Since t ∈ (a, b), {f = t} ⊆ A, so κ_j({f = t}) = κ_j({f = t} ∩ A) = (κ_j⌞A)({f = t}) = 0.
9. D_j(t) ≤ G_j(t). Put u_j(h) := ofReal(h⁻¹)·ν_j({t − h < f < t}). The sequence h_k tends to 0 through positive values, i.e. along atTop it tends to 0 within (0, ∞); a liminf along the finer filter (the image of atTop under k ↦ h_k) is at least the liminf along 𝓝[>] 0, so D_j(t) ≤ liminf_k u_j(h_k). For all k with h_k < t − a (all large k, since h_k → 0 < t − a): a < t − h_k and t < b give {t − h_k < f < t} ⊆ A, so ν_j({t − h_k < f < t}) = ν_j(f⁻¹((t − h_k, t)) ∩ A) = ρ_j((t − h_k, t)); and ofReal(h_k⁻¹) = k + 1. Hence u_j(h_k) = F_{j,k}(t) for all large k, and liminf_k u_j(h_k) = G_j(t). Therefore D_j(t) ≤ G_j(t).
10. (ii). D_j(t) ≤ G_j(t) < ∞ by steps 7 and 9.
11. (iii). liminf_j G_j(t) = H(t) = 0, so for every n ∈ ℕ there are infinitely many j with G_j(t) < 1/(n + 1). Choose φ(0) < φ(1) < ⋯ inductively with G_{φ(n)}(t) < 1/(n + 1) (Mathlib extraction_forall_of_frequently). Then 0 ≤ D_{φ(n)}(t) ≤ G_{φ(n)}(t) < 1/(n + 1) → 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Push ν_j⌞A forward by f to a finite measure ρ_j on ℝ; Tonelli on S_c = {s − c < y < s} gives ∫ ρ_j((s − c, s)) ds = c·ν_j(A).
G_j(s) := liminf_k (k + 1)·ρ_j((s − 1/(k + 1), s)) is Borel with ∫ G_j ≤ ν_j(A) (Fatou), so G_j < ∞ a.e.
Fatou in j: liminf_j G_j = 0 a.e.; for each j only countably many levels are atoms of κ_j⌞A.
Pick a good t ∈ (a, b): κ_j({f = t}) = 0, and D_j(t) ≤ G_j(t) < ∞ via h_k = 1/(k + 1) and {t − h_k < f < t} ⊆ A.
Extract φ with G_{φ(n)}(t) < 1/(n + 1), so D_{φ(n)}(t) → 0.

1. (Cut-off; parent step 2.) If K = ∅ put ψ := 0 and L := 0. Otherwise put δ := ε/2, ψ(x) := max{0, 1 − dist(x, K)/δ} and L := 1/δ. Then ψ is L-Lipschitz (x ↦ dist(x, K) is 1-Lipschitz, x ↦ 1 − dist(x, K)/δ is (1/δ)-Lipschitz, and taking the maximum with the constant 0 does not increase Lipschitz constants), 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1 and ψ = 1 on K. Let W₀ := {ψ > 0}. For K ≠ ∅, W₀ = {dist(·, K) < δ} is open, W₀ ⊆ thickening(ε, K) because δ < ε, and closure(W₀) ⊆ {dist(·, K) ≤ δ}, a closed and bounded, hence compact, subset of ℝ^P; for K = ∅, W₀ = ∅. In both cases W₀ is open, closure(W₀) is compact and W₀ ⊆ thickening(ε, K). Put f := −ψ (L-Lipschitz, continuous, hence Borel) and fix r₀ > 0 with closure(W₀) ⊆ B_{r₀}(0).
2. (Flat convergence; parent step 4.) Apply (FL′) to W₀: R_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}, S′_j ∈ 𝒟_n integer multiplicity with C − Ŝ_j − S′_j = ∂R_j and a_j := M_{W₀}(R_j) + M_{W₀}(S′_j) → 0. By (IMC)(c) twice, C − Ŝ_j − S′_j = ∂R_j is integer multiplicity. Choose IMReps ρ_j of R_j, β_j of ∂R_j, σ_j of S′_j (all in ℝ^P), and write μ_j := μ_{ρ_j}, μ′_j := μ_{β_j}.
3. (Slicing; parent step 5.) Fix j and apply (SL′) to T := R_j, μ := μ_j, ξ := ξ_{ρ_j}, μ′ := μ′_j, ξ′ := ξ_{β_j} and the L-Lipschitz f. Its hypotheses hold: μ_j and μ′_j are finite on compact sets (step 0); ξ_{ρ_j}, ξ_{β_j} are a.e. strongly measurable for μ_j, μ′_j by (IR)(b); by (IMC)(d) the bound |ξ_{ρ_j}(x)(α)| ≤ |α| (all α) holds H^{n+1}⌞M-a.e. on the carrier M of ρ_j, hence μ_j-a.e. since μ_j ≪ H^{n+1}⌞M by (IR)(a), and likewise for β_j; R_j(ω) = ρ_j.action(ω) = ∫ ξ_{ρ_j}(ω) dμ_j by (IR)(c) with E := ℝ^P and R′ := ρ_j (carrier M = M ∩ ℝ^P), and likewise ∂R_j(η) = ∫ ξ_{β_j}(η) dμ′_j. Obtain A_{j,t} ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}, B_{j,t} ∈ 𝒟_n (t ∈ ℝ) with the four properties of (SL′).
4. (Level and subsequence; parent step 5(c).) By (κ) choose j₁ with κ_j(B_{r₀}(0)) < ∞ for all j ≥ j₁. Apply (GL) with ν_j := μ_j⌞W₀, κ′_j := κ_{j+j₁}, the Borel function f and (a, b) := (−1, 0); the set A′ := {−1 < f < 0} = {0 < ψ < 1} is contained in W₀ ⊆ B_{r₀}(0). Hypotheses: ν_j(A′) ≤ μ_j(W₀) ≤ μ_j(closure W₀) < ∞ (step 0); ν_j(A′) ≤ μ_j(W₀) = M_{W₀}(R_j) ≤ a_j → 0 by (MR) (W₀ open), so ν_j(A′) → 0; κ′_j(A′) ≤ κ_{j+j₁}(B_{r₀}(0)) < ∞. (GL) gives t ∈ (−1, 0) and a strictly increasing φ with (i) κ_{k+j₁}({f = t}) = 0 for every k, (ii) D_j < ∞ for every j and (iii) D_{φ(k)} → 0, where D_j := liminf_{h→0⁺} h⁻¹ν_j({t − h < f < t}). Since W₀ is open (Borel), ν_j(s) = μ_j(s ∩ W₀) = μ_j(W₀ ∩ s) for every set s, so D_j = liminf_{h→0⁺} h⁻¹μ_j(W₀ ∩ {t − h < f < t}).
Put α := −t ∈ (0, 1), W := {f < t} = {ψ > α}, F := {f ≤ t} = {ψ ≥ α}, Σ := F ∖ W = {f = t} = {ψ = α}, and φ′(i) := φ(i + j₁).
5. (W, F, φ′.) W is open and F is closed (f continuous). F ⊆ W₀ (ψ ≥ α > 0 on F), so F ⊆ closure(W₀) is compact, and Σ is a compact subset of the open set W₀. K ⊆ W (ψ = 1 > α on K), W ⊆ F, and W ⊆ W₀ ⊆ thickening(ε, K). φ′ is strictly increasing, and φ′(i) ≥ i + j₁ ≥ j₁ (a strictly increasing map ℕ → ℕ satisfies φ(k) ≥ k); writing φ′(i) = (φ′(i) − j₁) + j₁, (i) gives κ_{φ′(i)}(F ∖ W) = κ_{φ′(i)}({f = t}) = 0.
6. (The currents of index i; parent step 6.) Fix i and put j := φ′(i). By (IMC)(b) applied to ρ_j, β_j, σ_j and the Borel set W there are IMReps ρ′_j, β′_j, σ′_j in ℝ^P with carriers (carrier) ∩ W, the same multiplicities and orientations, each representing a current. By (IR)(c): ρ′_j.action(ω) = ∫_W ξ_{ρ_j}(ω) dμ_j = A_{j,t}(ω), so ρ′_j represents A_{j,t} and A_{j,t} = R_j⌞W is integer multiplicity; β′_j.action(η) = ∫_W ξ_{β_j}(η) dμ′_j = B_{j,t}(η), so β′_j represents B_{j,t}, with μ_{β′_j} = μ′_j⌞W; and σ′_j represents a current S′_j⌞W with (S′_j⌞W)(ω) = ∫_W ξ_{σ_j}(ω) dμ_{σ_j} and μ_{σ′_j} = μ_{σ_j}⌞W. Define
 Ŷ_i := ∂A_{j,t}, P_i := ∂A_{j,t} − B_{j,t}, Sr_i := S′_j⌞W − P_i, e_i := M_{W₀}(S′_{φ′(i)}) + L·D_{φ′(i)}.
7. (Mass of P_i; parent step 5(a).) By (SL′), P_i(η) = ∂A_{j,t}(η) − B_{j,t}(η) = 0 whenever tsupport η ∩ Σ = ∅. Σ is compact and contained in the open set W₀, so (ML) gives M_G(P_i) ≤ M_{W₀}(P_i) for every set G, and (SL′) with W := W₀ gives M_{W₀}(P_i) ≤ L·D_j. Hence M_G(P_i) ≤ L·D_j < ∞ for every G (L < ∞ and (ii)).
8. (Ŷ_i is an integer multiplicity cycle; parent step 5(b).) For every η, ∂A_{j,t}(η) = B_{j,t}(η) + 1·P_i(η). For open G with compact closure, (MT), (MR) for β′_j and step 7 give M_G(∂A_{j,t}) ≤ M_G(B_{j,t}) + M_G(P_i) ≤ μ_{β′_j}(G) + L·D_j ≤ μ′_j(closure G) + L·D_j < ∞ (step 0). Since A_{j,t} is integer multiplicity (step 6), (BR′) shows that Ŷ_i = ∂A_{j,t} is integer multiplicity. ∂Ŷ_i = ∂∂A_{j,t} = 0.
9. (spt Ŷ_i ⊆ F.) Let x ∉ F. As F is closed there is r > 0 with B := B_r(x) disjoint from F; B is open with compact closure. If η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) has tsupport η ⊆ B, then tsupport dη ⊆ tsupport η ⊆ B misses W ⊆ F, so dη = 0 on W and Ŷ_i(η) = A_{j,t}(dη) = ∫_{f<t} ξ_{ρ_j}(dη) dμ_j = 0. So B lies in the zero region of Ŷ_i and x ∉ spt Ŷ_i.
10. (Mass of Sr_i; parent step 6.) Sr_i(ω) = (S′_j⌞W)(ω) + (−1)·P_i(ω) for all ω, so (MT) with c = −1, (MR) for σ′_j and step 7 give M(Sr_i) ≤ M(S′_j⌞W) + M(P_i) ≤ μ_{σ_j}(W) + L·D_j = M_W(S′_j) + L·D_j ≤ M_{W₀}(S′_j) + L·D_j = e_i, using (MR) for σ_j and the monotonicity of M_G in G.
11. (Measure of Ŷ_i on F ∖ W; ∂R̃-part of parent step 8(c).) Let R be an IMRep of Ŷ_i. Σ = F ∖ W is compact. For every open G ⊇ Σ with compact closure, (MR), (MT) and steps 7–8 give μ_R(G) = M_G(Ŷ_i) ≤ M_G(B_{j,t}) + M_G(P_i) ≤ μ_{β′_j}(G) + L·D_j. (COB) with U := ℝ^P, E := Σ, ν := μ_{β′_j} (finite on compact sets, step 0) and c := L·D_j gives μ_R(Σ) ≤ μ_{β′_j}(Σ) + L·D_j = μ′_j(Σ ∩ W) + L·D_j = L·D_j ≤ e_i, since Σ ∩ W = ∅.
12. (Identity on W; parent (★).) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. (a) Evaluating C − Ŝ_j − S′_j = ∂R_j at ω: C(ω) − Ŝ_j(ω) − S′_j(ω) = R_j(dω) = ∫ ξ_{ρ_j}(dω) dμ_j; as tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, the integrand vanishes off W = {f < t}, so this equals ∫_{f<t} ξ_{ρ_j}(dω) dμ_j = A_{j,t}(dω) = Ŷ_i(ω). (b) (S′_j⌞W)(ω) = ∫_W ξ_{σ_j}(ω) dμ_{σ_j} = ∫ ξ_{σ_j}(ω) dμ_{σ_j} = S′_j(ω), because ω = 0 off W ((IR)(c) with E := ℝ^P). (c) tsupport ω ⊆ W is disjoint from Σ, so P_i(ω) = 0 (step 7) and Sr_i(ω) = S′_j(ω). Therefore C(ω) = Ŝ_j(ω) + Ŷ_i(ω) + Sr_i(ω), with j = φ′(i).
13. (e_i → 0.) M_{W₀}(S′_{φ′(i)}) ≤ a_{φ′(i)} → 0 because φ′(i) → ∞; D_{φ′(i)} = D_{φ(i+j₁)} → 0 by (iii), so L·D_{φ′(i)} → 0 (L < ∞). Hence e_i → 0.
Steps 5–13 give all conclusions: W open, F compact, K ⊆ W ⊆ F, W ⊆ thickening(ε, K), φ′ strictly increasing, e_i → 0, and for every i the properties of Ŷ_i (steps 8, 9, 11), M(Sr_i) ≤ e_i (step 10), κ_{φ′(i)}(F ∖ W) = 0 (step 5) and the identity on W (step 12). ∎

The representing measures of R_j and ∂R_j satisfy the hypotheses of (SL′) (imrep_restriction, im_calculus (d)); slice R_j by f = −ψ.

P_i = ∂(R_j⌞W) − (∂R_j)⌞W: mass_localization and (SL′) give M(P_i) ≤ L·D_j; (BR′) makes Ŷ_i = ∂(R_j⌞W) an integer multiplicity cycle supported in F.
M(Sr_i) ≤ M_{W₀}(S′_j) + L·D_j and μ_{Ŷ_i}(F ∖ W) ≤ L·D_j (mass_triangle, compact_outer_bound); C = Ŝ_j + Ŷ_i + Sr_i on forms supported in W; e_i → 0.

subproblems.title: Almost-minimality under a retracted cycle modification (Simon 7.2.4 (8)–(9) with Remark 7.2.5(2); step 7 (I) of the parent)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, A ⊆ ℝ^P, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in A (contract IsMinimizingIn T A) with spt T ⊆ A. Let G, G₃, L ∈ ℝ with 0 < G ≤ G₃, closedBall(0, G₃) ⊆ U and M_{B_{G₃}(0)}(T) < ∞. Let π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be C¹ on B_{2G}(0) (ContDiffOn ℝ 1), with π(B_{2G}(0)) ⊆ A ∩ B_{G₃}(0), π(y) = y for every y ∈ A ∩ B_{2G}(0), and ‖Dπ(y)‖ ≤ L (operator norm of fderiv) for every y ∈ B_{2G}(0). Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with ∂Y = 0 and spt Y compact and contained in B_G(0), and let Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy Z(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (Y evaluated on the same form regarded as a test form on ℝ^P, testFormOnInclusion). Assume the push-forward theorem (PF) for (P, m): for every open O ⊆ ℝ^P, every f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P that is C¹ on O and every c ∈ ℝ with ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ c for y ∈ O, there is a map push : 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that (A) for every X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with spt X compact and contained in O and every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) of X in ℝ^P: (i) push X(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x)) ∘ Λⁿ Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), (ii) push X is integer multiplicity, (iii) spt(push X) ⊆ f(spt X), (iv) M(push X) ≤ cⁿ·M(X) (ENNReal.ofReal(cⁿ)), (v) ∂X = 0 implies ∂(push X) = 0, (vi) if f(y) = y for every y ∈ spt X then push X = X; and (B) push(X₁ − X₂) = push X₁ − push X₂ for all integer multiplicity X₁, X₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with compact supports contained in O. Then M_{B_G(0)}(T) ≤ Lⁿ·M_{B_G(0)}(Z) in [0, ∞] (Lⁿ read as ENNReal.ofReal(Lⁿ)).

Source: parent proof, step 7, case (P), items (a)–(e), up to the inequality (I) (Simon 7.2.4 (8)–(9), chapter-07.txt lines 220–246, modified as indicated in Remark 7.2.5(2), lines 165–174: competitors are pushed into A by the retraction π). Specialization: (I) is stated for masses, M_{B_G}(T) ≤ Lⁿ M_{B_G}(Z) with Z = T + Y; the parent's identification μ_{Q+Y}(B_G) = μ_{S_j+Y}(B_G) through (F2) is replaced by the direct inequality M_{B_G}(Q + Y) ≤ M_{B_G}(Z) (the two currents agree on forms supported in B_G), and the parent's μ_{Q+Y}(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) = 0 is proved by splitting ℝ^P ∖ B_G into the open set ℝ^P ∖ B̄_G and the compact sphere.
Siblings: (VO) vanish_off_support; (MR) mass_and_support; (IMC) im_calculus ((b) restriction, (c) differences, (d) orientation bound); (RO) restrict_open_im; (IR) imrep_restriction; (MT) mass_triangle; (COB) compact_outer_bound.
Conventions. B_r := B_r(0), B̄_r := closedBall(0, r), S_G := {x : |x| = G}. A test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is also regarded as an element of 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (same form; testFormOnInclusion), and for X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), X|_U := X.restrictDomain(U ⊆ ℝ^P), so X|_U(ω) = X(ω). For an IMRep R write μ_R := R.measure, ξ_R := R.orient. Note B̄_G ⊆ B̄_{G₃} ⊆ U, B̄_G ⊆ B_{2G} (G > 0) and B_G ⊆ B_{G₃}.
Preliminaries.
(p1) If X is a current in an open V and X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ G, then M_G(X) = 0 (every term of the supremum is ofReal 0), and, if G is open and R is an IMRep of X, μ_R(G) = 0 by (MR).
(p2) (Support from vanishing.) If X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), E ⊆ ℝ^P is closed and X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ E = ∅, then spt X ⊆ E: a point x ∉ E has a ball B_r(x) disjoint from E, an open set with compact closure on which X vanishes, so x lies in the zero region. spt X is closed; if E is compact, spt X is compact.
(p3) (Sums.) For an integer multiplicity X in an open V, X − X = 0 is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c); hence for integer multiplicity X, X′ in V, 0 − X′ and X + X′ := X − (0 − X′) are integer multiplicity, and (X + X′)(ω) = X(ω) + X′(ω).
(p4) (Restriction.) If X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), then M_G(X|_U) ≤ M_G(X) for every G: a form admissible for M_G(X|_U) is admissible for M_G(X), with the same value.
(p5) (Local finiteness.) For an IMRep R in an open V and compact K′ ⊆ V, μ_R(K′) = ∫_{M∩K′} θ dHⁿ < ∞.
(p6) (Boundaries.) ∂(X − X′) = ∂X − ∂X′ and ∂(X|_U) = (∂X)|_U, by evaluation on dη.
1. (Push-forward.) Apply (PF) with O := B_{2G}, f := π, c := L, and obtain push. Fix an IMRep R_T = (M_T, θ_T, ξ_T) of T in U (T is integer multiplicity by minimality) and write μ_T := μ_{R_T}.
2. (The current Q := T⌞B_G in ℝ^P.) By (IMC)(b) in U with E := B_G there is an IMRep R₁ in U with carrier M_T ∩ B_G, multiplicity θ_T and orientation ξ_T; by (IR)(c), μ_{R₁} = μ_T⌞B_G and R₁.action(ω) = ∫_{B_G} ξ_T(ω) dμ_T for every n-form ω. The same carrier, multiplicity and orientation form an IMRep R₂ in ℝ^P: the fields of IMRep other than carrier ⊆ U and local integrability do not involve U; the carrier lies in ℝ^P; and for compact K′, ∫_{M_T∩B_G∩K′} θ_T dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M_T∩B̄_G} θ_T dHⁿ < ∞ because B̄_G is a compact subset of U. By (IMC)(b) in ℝ^P with E := ℝ^P there is a current Q ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) represented by an IMRep R₃ with the same carrier (∩ ℝ^P), multiplicity and orientation. Hence Q is integer multiplicity, Q(ω) = R₁.action(ω) = ∫_{B_G} ξ_T(ω) dμ_T for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), and μ_{R₃}(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) = 0 (its carrier lies in B_G).
 (Q1) If tsupport ω ⊆ B_G, then Q(ω) = T(ω): T(ω) = R_T.action(ω) = ∫ ξ_T(ω) dμ_T ((IR)(c), E := ℝ^P), and ω = 0 off B_G.
 (Q2) If tsupport ω ∩ B̄_G = ∅, then Q(ω) = 0, since ω = 0 on B_G.
 (Q3) spt Q ⊆ B̄_G ∩ spt T, and spt Q is compact. Let x ∉ B̄_G ∩ spt T. If x ∉ B̄_G, (Q2) and the argument of (p2) give x ∉ spt Q. If x ∈ B̄_G ∖ spt T, then x ∈ U ∖ spt T, so x lies in an open V with compact closure in U on which T vanishes; μ_T(V) = 0 by (p1); for ω with tsupport ω ⊆ V the integrand ξ_T(ω)·1_{B_G} vanishes off the μ_T-null set V, so Q(ω) = 0; hence x is in the zero region of Q. spt Q is closed and contained in the compact set B̄_G, hence compact.
 (Q4) spt Q ⊆ B̄_G ∩ spt T ⊆ B_{2G} ∩ A, where π is the identity. Q is admissible for (PF) and push Q = Q by (PF)(vi).
3. (Push of Y.) Y is admissible: integer multiplicity, spt Y compact and ⊆ B_G ⊆ O. By (PF): push Y is integer multiplicity, ∂(push Y) = 0, and spt(push Y) ⊆ π(spt Y) ⊆ π(B_{2G}) ⊆ A ∩ B_{G₃}. π is continuous on O (C¹) and spt Y ⊆ O is compact, so π(spt Y) is compact; spt(push Y) is closed and contained in it, hence compact; and spt(push Y) ⊆ B_{G₃} ⊆ U.
4. (Q + Y.) Put QY := Q − (0 − Y); it is integer multiplicity (p3) and QY(ω) = Q(ω) + Y(ω). If tsupport ω ∩ B̄_G = ∅ then Q(ω) = 0 by (Q2) and Y(ω) = 0 by (VO) (spt Y ⊆ B_G), so by (p2) spt QY ⊆ B̄_G is compact and contained in O. The currents 0 and 0 − Y are admissible: they are integer multiplicity (p3), spt 0 = ∅, and spt(0 − Y) = spt Y (both vanish on the same forms). By (PF)(B): push 0 = push(0 − 0) = push 0 − push 0, hence push 0 = 0 (evaluate at each ω); push(0 − Y) = push 0 − push Y = 0 − push Y; and push QY = push Q − push(0 − Y) = Q − (0 − push Y). So push QY(ω) = Q(ω) + push Y(ω) for every ω, and, QY being integer multiplicity, (PF)(iv) gives M(push QY) ≤ Lⁿ M(QY).
5. (The competitor.) (push Y)|_U is integer multiplicity by (RO) (U open), and Z₁ := T − (0 − (push Y)|_U) ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is integer multiplicity by (p3), with Z₁(ω) = T(ω) + push Y(ω).
 (i) ∂Z₁ = ∂T by (p6) and ∂(push Y) = 0; so SameBoundary Z₁ T.
 (ii) (Z₁ − T)(ω) = push Y(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). If x ∈ U ∖ spt(push Y), push Y vanishes on an open V ∋ x; choosing r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ⊆ U, the open set V ∩ B_r(x) has compact closure in U and Z₁ − T vanishes on it. Hence spt(Z₁ − T) ⊆ spt(push Y) ⊆ A ∩ B_{G₃}.
 (iii) spt(Z₁ − T) = U ∖ (zero region) is relatively closed in U and contained in the compact set spt(push Y) ⊆ U, so it equals spt(push Y) minus an open set and is compact.
 (iv) W′ := B_{G₃} is open and closure(W′) ⊆ B̄_{G₃} ⊆ U is compact (CompactlyContained W′ U).
 By minimality of T in A (with W′ and the competitor Z₁), M_{B_{G₃}}(T) ≤ M_{B_{G₃}}(Z₁).
6. (Upper bound for Z₁.) By (IMC)(b) in U with E := ℝ^P ∖ B_G there is a current T₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by an IMRep R₄ with carrier M_T ∖ B_G; by (IR)(c), μ_{R₄} = μ_T⌞(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) and T₁(ω) = ∫_{ℝ^P∖B_G} ξ_T(ω) dμ_T. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function ξ_T(ω) is μ_T-integrable: it is μ_T-a.e. strongly measurable ((IR)(b), ω continuous), bounded μ_T-a.e. by sup_x|ω(x)| < ∞ ((IMC)(d) and (IR)(a)), and vanishes off the compact set tsupport ω ⊆ U, which has finite μ_T-measure (p5). So T(ω) = ∫ ξ_T(ω) dμ_T = ∫_{B_G} ξ_T(ω) dμ_T + ∫_{ℝ^P∖B_G} ξ_T(ω) dμ_T = Q(ω) + T₁(ω), and therefore Z₁(ω) = T₁(ω) + (push QY)|_U(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). (MT) with c = 1, (MR) for T₁ and (p4) give
 M_{B_{G₃}}(Z₁) ≤ M_{B_{G₃}}(T₁) + M_{B_{G₃}}((push QY)|_U) ≤ μ_T(B_{G₃} ∖ B_G) + M(push QY) ≤ μ_T(B_{G₃} ∖ B_G) + Lⁿ M(QY).
7. (Cancellation.) By (MR), M_{B_{G₃}}(T) = μ_T(B_{G₃}) = μ_T(B_G) + μ_T(B_{G₃} ∖ B_G), and this is finite by hypothesis. Steps 5 and 6 give μ_T(B_G) + μ_T(B_{G₃} ∖ B_G) ≤ μ_T(B_{G₃} ∖ B_G) + Lⁿ M(QY); cancelling the finite term, M_{B_G}(T) = μ_T(B_G) ≤ Lⁿ M(QY) ((MR) again).
8. (M(QY) ≤ M_{B_G}(Z).) Let R_{QY} be an IMRep of QY and R_Y one of Y. By (MR), M(QY) = μ_{R_{QY}}(ℝ^P) = μ_{R_{QY}}(B_G) + μ_{R_{QY}}(S_G) + μ_{R_{QY}}(ℝ^P ∖ B̄_G).
 (a) QY vanishes on forms supported in the open set ℝ^P ∖ B̄_G (step 4), so μ_{R_{QY}}(ℝ^P ∖ B̄_G) = 0 by (p1).
 (b) For every open G′ ⊇ S_G with compact closure, (MR) and (MT) with c = 1 give μ_{R_{QY}}(G′) = M_{G′}(QY) ≤ M_{G′}(Q) + M_{G′}(Y) = μ_{R₃}(G′) + μ_{R_Y}(G′). (COB) with U := ℝ^P, the compact set E := S_G, ν := μ_{R₃} + μ_{R_Y} (finite on compact sets, (p5)) and c := 0 gives μ_{R_{QY}}(S_G) ≤ μ_{R₃}(S_G) + μ_{R_Y}(S_G). Here μ_{R₃}(S_G) = 0 (carrier of R₃ ⊆ B_G); and Y vanishes on forms supported in the open set ℝ^P ∖ spt Y (VO), so μ_{R_Y}(ℝ^P ∖ spt Y) = 0 by (p1), while S_G ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ spt Y because spt Y ⊆ B_G. So μ_{R_{QY}}(S_G) = 0.
 (c) μ_{R_{QY}}(B_G) = M_{B_G}(QY) by (MR). If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) is admissible for M_{B_G}(QY), then, as tsupport ω ⊆ B_G ⊆ U, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is admissible for M_{B_G}(Z) and QY(ω) = Q(ω) + Y(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ω) = Z(ω) by (Q1). Hence M_{B_G}(QY) ≤ M_{B_G}(Z).
 So M(QY) ≤ M_{B_G}(Z), and step 7 gives M_{B_G}(T) ≤ Lⁿ M_{B_G}(Z). ∎

Conventions. B_r := B_r(0), B̄_r := closedBall(0, r); a test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is also regarded as an element of 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (testFormOnInclusion); for X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), X|_U := X.restrictDomain(U ⊆ ℝ^P), so X|_U(ω) = X(ω); μ_T := μ_R; Σ := F ∖ W (compact: F compact, W open) and O′ := B_G ∖ F (open: F closed). Preliminaries.
(p1) If a current X in an open V satisfies X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ G, then M_G(X) = 0, and, if G is open and R′ is an IMRep of X, μ_{R′}(G) = 0 by (MR).
(p2) If X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), E ⊆ ℝ^P is closed and X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ E = ∅, then spt X ⊆ E (each x ∉ E has a ball disjoint from E, an open set with compact closure on which X vanishes); if E is compact, spt X is compact.
(p3) For integer multiplicity X, X′ in an open V: X − X = 0 is integer multiplicity ((IMC)(c)); hence 0 − X′ and X + X′ := X − (0 − X′) are integer multiplicity, with (X + X′)(ω) = X(ω) + X′(ω).
(p4) For X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and every G, M_G(X|_U) ≤ M_G(X) (admissible forms for X|_U are admissible for X, with the same values).
(p5) For an IMRep R′ in an open V and compact K′ ⊆ V, μ_{R′}(K′) < ∞ (field locallyIntegrable_mult).
(p6) ∂(X − X′) = ∂X − ∂X′ and ∂(X|_U) = (∂X)|_U (evaluate on dη).
1. (Case A ∩ B_{2G} = ∅; parent case (E).) Then spt T ∩ B_{2G} = ∅ because spt T ⊆ A. If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ F ⊆ B_G ⊆ B_{2G}, then tsupport ω ∩ spt T = ∅, so T(ω) = 0 by (VO). By (p1), M_W(T) = 0, and the claim holds. From now on assume the second alternative: π is C¹ on B_{2G}, maps B_{2G} into A ∩ B_{G₃}, fixes A ∩ B_{2G}, and ‖Dπ‖ ≤ L on B_{2G}.
2. (The cycle Y; parent step 7.) X := S − C is integer multiplicity ((IMC)(c)), ∂X = ∂S − ∂C = 0 (p6) and spt X ⊆ W. Y := X − (0 − Ŷ) (= X + Ŷ) is integer multiplicity (p3) and ∂Y = ∂X + ∂Ŷ = 0 (p6). If tsupport ω ∩ F = ∅, then X(ω) = 0 and Ŷ(ω) = 0 by (VO) (spt X ⊆ W ⊆ F and spt Ŷ ⊆ F), so Y(ω) = 0; by (p2) spt Y ⊆ F, so spt Y is compact and contained in B_G.
3. (Comparison current and (I).) Y|_U is integer multiplicity by (RO), so Z := T − (0 − Y|_U) ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is integer multiplicity (p3), and Z(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). The hypotheses of (RC) hold for (U, A, T, Z, Y, π, G, G₃, L) and (PF): 0 < G ≤ G₃, closedBall(0, G₃) ⊆ U, M_{B_{G₃}}(T) < ∞, the properties of π, Y integer multiplicity with ∂Y = 0 and spt Y compact ⊆ B_G, and the identity for Z. (RC) gives
 (I) M_{B_G}(T) ≤ Lⁿ·M_{B_G}(Z).
4. (Decomposition; parent step 8.) B_G is the disjoint union of the Borel sets W, Σ and O′ (W ⊆ F ⊆ B_G). Let R_Z be an IMRep of Z. By (MR), M_{B_G}(T) = μ_T(B_G) = μ_T(W) + μ_T(Σ) + μ_T(O′) = μ_T(W) + μ_T(O′), since μ_T(Σ) = μ_R(F ∖ W) = 0; and M_{B_G}(Z) = μ_{R_Z}(W) + μ_{R_Z}(Σ) + μ_{R_Z}(O′).
5. (On O′; parent 8(b).) If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has tsupport ω ⊆ O′, then tsupport ω ∩ F = ∅, so Y(ω) = 0 (step 2) and Z(ω) = T(ω) + 1·0(ω), 0 the zero current of U. (MT) gives M_{O′}(Z) ≤ M_{O′}(T) + M_{O′}(0) = M_{O′}(T), so μ_{R_Z}(O′) ≤ μ_T(O′) by (MR) (O′ open).
6. (On Σ; parent 8(c).) Let R_X, R_Ŷ be IMReps of X, Ŷ in ℝ^P. For every open G′ ⊇ Σ with compact closure in U, (MR), (MT) (in U for Z = T + Y|_U, in ℝ^P for Y = X + Ŷ) and (p4) give
 μ_{R_Z}(G′) = M_{G′}(Z) ≤ M_{G′}(T) + M_{G′}(Y|_U) ≤ M_{G′}(T) + M_{G′}(X) + M_{G′}(Ŷ) = μ_T(G′) + μ_{R_X}(G′) + μ_{R_Ŷ}(G′).
 ν := μ_T + μ_{R_X} + μ_{R_Ŷ} is finite on compact subsets of U (p5), and Σ ⊆ B_G ⊆ U is compact; (COB) with c := 0 gives μ_{R_Z}(Σ) ≤ μ_T(Σ) + μ_{R_X}(Σ) + μ_{R_Ŷ}(Σ). Here μ_T(Σ) = 0; X vanishes on forms supported in the open set ℝ^P ∖ spt X (VO), so μ_{R_X}(ℝ^P ∖ spt X) = 0 by (p1), and Σ ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ spt X because spt X ⊆ W and Σ ∩ W = ∅; and μ_{R_Ŷ}(Σ) ≤ e by hypothesis. Hence μ_{R_Z}(Σ) ≤ e.
7. (On W; parent 8(d).) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Since ω is a test form with tsupport in U, currentEval(T, ω) = T(ω), and the hypothesis gives C(ω) = T(ω) + Ŷ(ω) + Sr(ω). Hence Z(ω) = T(ω) + X(ω) + Ŷ(ω) = T(ω) + S(ω) − C(ω) + Ŷ(ω) = S(ω) − Sr(ω) = S|_U(ω) + (−1)·Sr|_U(ω).  a + b ≤ λ(s + e + e + b) = λ(s + 2e) + λb.
